subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should valid ignore files below the 4 MiB byte cap be terminally excluded when they exceed the proposed pattern-count or single-pattern-length limits?
rationale: This changes existing workspace-discovery semantics rather than only bounding memory use; source review cannot determine whether hiding user content is the intended compatibility contract.

options.title: Bound bytes only
options.body: Remove the pattern-count and pattern-length fail-closed paths, retaining the 4 MiB bounded read and oversized-file terminal exclusion.

options.title: Adopt complexity limits
options.body: Keep the new limits only with explicit owner approval, documented compatibility behavior, and exact-head proof showing the intended discovery impact.

recommendation.title: Bound bytes only
recommendation.body: Remove the pattern-count and pattern-length fail-closed paths, retaining the 4 MiB bounded read and oversized-file terminal exclusion.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent behavioral commits and current assignment connect steipete to this scan-policy decision.
